justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modest upward drift in gold prices from what I'd assume was a baseline around $2,100–$2,110 at the time of the forecast. At the one-day horizon, the estimate of $2,115 was anchored heavily on near-term price momentum and the absence of any imminent major catalysts, suggesting prices would stay close to their recent level with only slight drift. At the one-week horizon, the slight nudge to $2,125 reflected the general underlying bid for gold driven by persistent central bank buying, geopolitical uncertainty, and real rate dynamics that had been supportive of the metal. At the one-month horizon, the $2,150 estimate incorporated a mild bullish lean based on expectations that the Federal Reserve would be navigating a potential rate-cutting cycle, which historically weakens the dollar and supports gold as a non-yielding safe haven asset.

The confidence interval widths reflect fundamentally different uncertainty profiles across the three horizons. At one day, the tight $60 range ($2,055–$2,175) reflects that intraday and overnight gold markets tend to be relatively stable absent a shock, with most of the variance coming from unexpected macroeconomic data releases or geopolitical headlines. At one week, the interval widens to $230, accounting for a full week of trading sessions, any scheduled central bank communications, and potential shifts in currency markets. At one month, the $540 range reflects the substantial uncertainty around Fed policy signals, inflation data prints, dollar movements, and the evolving global risk environment — all of which can interact in complex and nonlinear ways to move gold meaningfully in either direction.

There are several tail risks that could push outcomes outside these stated intervals. On the upside, a sudden escalation in geopolitical conflict — particularly involving major energy-producing regions or a broader military confrontation — could trigger a sharp safe-haven rush that sends gold well above $2,420 within the month. A surprise deterioration in U.S. economic data causing markets to rapidly price in aggressive Fed cuts could also produce a stronger-than-expected rally. On the downside, an unexpectedly hawkish Fed pivot, a strong U.S. jobs report reversing rate-cut expectations, or a sudden liquidation event in risk assets forcing investors to sell gold for margin could push prices below $1,880. Currency dynamics, particularly a sharp dollar rally, represent another mechanism through which gold could underperform the lower bound of my monthly interval.
